voice.summary: Leland sounds like a smart friend who has done the thing and is telling you how: short sentences, a named school or company or number in nearly every line, and warmth that comes from inviting you in ("Come ask.") rather than from adjectives. Brand surfaces stay flat and confident with no exclamation points; the energy lives in founder and employee posts, in real customer quotes, and in the specificity of the detail.
rules: Lead with the point. "Today we launched Leland Community." not "Thrilled to announce" (house-style; Social Kit words-to-avoid).
Name it: the school, the company, the number, the person. "Google, Meta and Goldman" beats "top companies" every time (Social Kit idea 5; marketing-copy-guide).
Sell what they'll be able to do and how fast. "Become an AI Builder in 6-10 weeks", "about two hours", "from 2 hours to 30 minutes" (marketing-copy-guide core promise; case-study posts).
Numbers are real or absent. Never quote the sample numbers in the graphics or videos; never round a profile stat up (Social Kit guardrails; marketing-copy-guide).

No exclamation points and no em dashes in Leland's own copy. Verbatim quotes keep theirs (house-style). Founder and employee LinkedIn posts run warmer, and the kit allows it ("let the energy show"), so strip the punctuation when you move a team post onto a brand surface.
Warm comes from the invitation: come ask, follow along, send this to someone, the door's open. Not from community-speak like join our community or find your tribe (Social Kit voice).
Lead with learning from people who've done it. Meeting peers is a bonus, not the headline (Social Kit guardrails).
Don't call Community AI-powered, personalized or algorithmic, and don't name LinkedIn as the comparison in public posts (Social Kit guardrails).

Say expert, never coach, in anything new. The team still says coach in Slack and Nick edited "mentors" to "coaches" in-product on 10-19, so copy from Slack with care (BRAND-BRIEF; Mike Mella in #brand 2026-06-11).

The first line is the hook and the logo waits. A face beats a graphic, an opinion beats an announcement, a question beats a statement (Michael L via Vica 2026-01-30; Vica 2025-10-08; John on the jobs video 2026-10-22; John 2025-06-09).
Headlines are sentence case, 4 to 8 words, no period unless the period is the move ("Walk away certified.") (house-style; marketing-copy-guide).

First-touch email is friendly, not aggressive: "Welcome to Leland 👋" doubled opens over "Meet the experts getting customers into HBS, GSB and Wharton"; the CTA names the action, "Join Your First GRE Livestream" (Christian, #email 2026-08-16 and 2026-08-27).

items.text:
One of our AI Builder Program alumni lost his sales engineer. So he built one.

Mike works in sales at a company that partners with brands selling on Amazon. Every new prospect needed hours of research: revenue, pricing, growth, storefront, top sellers. When their sales engineer left, that work had nowhere to go.

So Mike built a tool his team calls Target. You type in any Amazon brand and it:
- Pulls trailing 12 month revenue, average selling price, growth vs category and top sellers
- Builds a fully designed scorecard deck with sales talking points, as a PowerPoint or PDF
- Finds the brand's key contacts and drafts outreach tailored to each person's role

All in about five seconds. It used to take hours.

This is what we mean when we say everyone is a builder now.

If you want to help your Sales & Business Development team get set up for this next chapter of AI change, let's chat.

items.text:
The team behind the ASU+GSV Summit just put 33 people through the AI Builder Program.

Partnerships, marketing and programs team. All building together.

Before, most of the team used AI for simple productivity stuff. Now they're building real systems. A few things they built:

- Lucy Baldwin (VP, Product) built a meeting prep system her team triggers from Slack. It researches every attendee, writes the prep doc and sends the calendar invite. ~8 hours a week of prep automated in busy season.
- Uma Sankar Reddy, a civil engineer by training, built a daily Slack digest that pulls to-dos from Slack, Airtable, Granola and email. It freed up 50% of Uma's time, enough to take on a second role.
- Genny Velazquez (SVP, Global Partnerships) built a proposal generator that writes in her voice. Proposals went from 2 hours to 30 minutes. That's 7.5 hours back every week.

Lucy said it best:

"It put everyone in a builder mindset."

That's the whole point of the AI Builder Program. It's not a learning experience, it's a building experience.

Shout out to Lucy, Uma, Genny and the whole ASU+GSV team.

If you want to help your team get set up for this next chapter of AI change, let's chat.

PlayPower marketing team had a project they'd been putting off for years.

1,500+ product spec sheets that needed to be rebuilt. At 8 to 15 minutes a sheet, it was scoped at 12 months. As Ryan Moats, their VP of Global Marketing, put it: "We're never going to get through that."

They got it done in weeks.

Their marketing team pulled data scattered across multiple systems into one spreadsheet, then had Claude generate every sheet. Then they kept going: a weekly competitive report that saves 6 to 8 hours, and ad campaigns bringing in more qualified leads.

My favorite part is the mindset shift. Ryan said the old excuse of "no resources or bandwidth" is almost gone.

Super fun to watch teams like this build. Proud they learned it in our AI Builder Program.

Shout out to Ryan and the whole PlayPower marketing team!

items.text:
Introducing... the fastest growing product Leland has ever launched:

The AI Builder Program.

If you have been feeling behind, overwhelmed, excited, scared, or anything else about AI, this is for you:

AI Builder Program (AIBP) Overview
- A 5-Level Program, taught live, online, by leading AI Instructors.
- Each Level is 6-sessions, taught over a condensed 3-week period, and focused on tangible impact and progress.
- The program will teach you all the most up-to-date and in-demand tools (Claude Code, n8n, Cowork, and more).

Each level of the program builds directly on the last. By the end of the program you will build workflows, agents, systems that run, self-correct, and improve on their own.

1. Level 1 teaches you to build AI skills and workflows that automate research, communication, and analysis.
2. Level 2 is where you build agents and agent teams to help you complete multi-step processes across tools.
3. Level 3 takes those agents and embeds them in systems that trigger and run on their own.
4. Level 4 focuses on orchestrating multiple agents in a unified system so they coordinate, delegate, and check each other's work.
5. Level 5 builds a goal-directed system with memory and self-correction loops.

The program is designed for non-technical knowledge workers of all AI skill levels.

Our next cohorts begin April 21, and will fill up, so we encourage you to join quickly. I have a limited number of discount codes, so if you are interested, shoot me a DM. I recommend starting with Level 1.

We've also sold several companies and enterprises on team access to this program, so if you think your company might be interested, shoot me a DM and we can talk more about group discounts.

AI is not coming. It is here. And the teams and individuals who adopt it are becoming 10x, 100x, and eventually 1,000x more impactful. The AIBP is just one step in a series of big announcements we'll be making over the coming months to ensure humans are brought along in this AI wave.

Reach out if you'd like the link to learn more (and want a discount).

items.text:
Share Your Livestream Clips in Community

Last week we introduced livestream clips, and we told you more was coming. Well, here it is! Starting this week, you can post your clips directly to Community.

Every livestream has moments worth sharing: the question everyone asks, the story about your own journey, the advice you give on every intro call. Clips pull those moments out for you, and now you can get them in front of the people who need them, right inside Leland.

How it works

- Open any past livestream in your livestreams dashboard to see your clips.
- Click Share on a clip and select Post to Leland. We'll start a post with the clip attached, so all you need to add is a sentence of context.
- Or start from the feed: open the composer on your Community home and choose Share a clip.

Clips play right in the feed and show up in the Activity tab on your profile, so prospective clients who find you later will see them too.

Why this matters for you

Most people in Community aren't ready to book yet. A one-hour recording is a big ask at that stage, but a 30-second clip is an easy way to show them what it's like to work with you. We've already seen experts get booked after customers found them through Community posts, and clips make it much easier to post consistently without extra time on camera.

Try this week: Post one clip from your most recent livestream with a quick note on who it's for. Then make it a habit!

Don't see clips on a past livestream? It may predate the beta. Host a new livestream with recording upload enabled and your clips will be ready shortly after. And keep using the thumbs up/down on each clip, it helps us learn which ones are worth sharing!
items.source: Slack #launch-events, Jake Evans, 2026-10-27 (approved by Ella Hess, posted to expert Slack by Chandler)
